purpose: Reproducible preparation of public human-written parallel correction data for an offline English/German contextual edit experiment.
publication_status: Raw and derived learner text stays outside the repository pending a separate privacy and redistribution review. A public repository license is evidence of terms, not a guarantee that every learner detail is safe to republish.

sources.license_evidence: LICENSE in pinned repository, copyright 2022 YUAN Xun, includes repository data without a separate data exclusion.
sources.citation: Xun Yuan, Derek Pham, Sam Davidson, Zhou Yu. 2022. ErAConD: Error Annotated Conversational Dialog Dataset for Grammatical Error Correction. NAACL, pages 76-84.
sources.selection: All data/*/orig/*.txt aligned by line with data/*/corr/*.txt. corr2 is an alternative annotation and is excluded. Each orig file is a conversation. Preserve original strings; each pair is an utterance and may contain more than one sentence.
sources.annotation_limits: Corrected text includes capitalization, punctuation, vocabulary and fluency edits, which do not all match a conservative typo-only policy. Published paper reports 1735 user turns; pinned source contains 1732 aligned lines in 186 conversations.
sources.privacy_evidence: The paper's Ethical Considerations states that annotators anonymized personally identifiable information and removed potentially offensive content. This does not substitute for redistribution review.

sources.license_evidence: Root LICENSE is CC BY-SA 4.0; README Data Licenses supplies component data licenses. scripts/LICENSE is GPL-3.0; repository scripts are not executed or incorporated.
sources.citation: Adriane Boyd. 2018. Using Wikipedia Edits in Low Resource Grammatical Error Correction. WNUT 2018.

sources.license: Component licenses below; archive data/LICENSE is CC-BY-SA-4.0
sources.selection: Only data/source/falko-id-ctok-zh1.txt.* and merlin-id-ctok-zh1.txt.*. Original provided train/dev/test partitions are pooled then split by source document hash. No Wikipedia text or experimental scripts are used. Original tokenized ctok and ZH1/TH1 strings are preserved exactly.

components.attribution: Falko corpus creators, Humboldt-Universitaet zu Berlin; conversion and sentence/text-ID alignment by Adriane Boyd.
components.evidence: Pinned Boyd README Data Licenses. Original corpus web page returned an anti-bot challenge on verification; its terms were not independently re-read.

components.attribution: MERLIN corpus project and creators; conversion and sentence/text-ID alignment by Adriane Boyd.
components.evidence: Pinned Boyd README Data Licenses and archive license. Original repository returned an access-denied anti-bot page on verification.
Pinned Boyd README. Wikipedia data is present in the downloaded archive but never extracted by the preparation script or used.

sources.privacy_limits: Public learner texts include names, addresses and email-like strings, some from fictional prompts. Raw or derived text must not be committed without a separate review.

split.algorithm: int(SHA256('localcorrect-context-v1\0' + document_id)[:8],16) modulo 100; 0..79 train, 80..89 calibration, 90..99 test
split.document_units: ErAConD conversation file; Falko/MERLIN original text ID
split.normalization: Unicode NFKC, casefold, retain only Unicode alphanumeric characters. Used only for conservative duplicate detection, never to alter model text.
split.cross_split_policy: Remove every pair whose normalized input or normalized expected appears in any other split. Input and expected share a key namespace, so input-to-expected leakage is also removed. Log all collision IDs and original splits, without copying learner text into audit messages.
split.within_split_policy: Collapse repeated normalized input/expected pairs deterministically. Remove normalized inputs with conflicting normalized expected values. Keep removed-ID audit. No holdout result is used in selection.
